about.metaTitle: About Rocket Draft — Fan-Made RLCS Draft Game
about.metaDescription: Rocket Draft is a free, fan-made RLCS draft game by LiberatoRL. Draft real Rocket League esports lineups from 2016 to today, build chemistry and win the bracket.
about.title: About Rocket Draft
about.intro: Rocket Draft is a free, fan-made RLCS draft game — a Rocket League esports roster builder that turns the history of the scene into a playable draft. Here is what it is, who made it, and why it exists.

sections.heading: What is Rocket Draft
sections.body: Rocket Draft is a free Rocket League esports roster builder. Each round deals one real historical RLCS lineup from 2016 to today, and you take a single card — a player, the coach, the substitute, or the organization — until you have three players, one coach, one sub, and one org. Then you build chemistry, collect special cards, and run an RLCS-style tournament. No account, no download — it plays in any browser, desktop or mobile.

sections.heading: Why it exists and who made it
sections.body: Rocket Draft was created by LiberatoRL, a fan, as an unofficial passion project celebrating RLCS history, with the player overalls reviewed and balanced by GWR. It is non-commercial and free, with a Discord community and a buy-me-a-coffee support link for anyone who wants to help keep it running. Credit where it is due: the game is inspired by Rams' draftrlcs.app. It exists because RLCS history deserves a way to be replayed, not just remembered.

sections.heading: What makes it different
sections.body: Two things set Rocket Draft apart. The first is Region-Locked Draft: North America, Europe, South America (SAM), MENA and Oceania each have their own pool, hand-researched from Liquipedia — a scene's World Championship rosters plus the regional teams that never reached Worlds, with deeper benches and cult underdogs like yanxnz. The second is transparent ratings: every overall is a calculated base plus a hand manual review, reviewed over time, and open to community pushback.

sections.heading: A fan project, not affiliated
sections.body: Rocket Draft is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with Psyonix, Epic Games, or any esports organization, and Rocket League is a trademark of its owners. Everything here is built out of respect for the players, teams, and moments that shaped the scene. Want to dive in? Head to How to Play to learn the loop, or jump straight into Play.

faq.metaTitle: Rocket Draft FAQ — RLCS Draft Game Questions Answered
faq.metaDescription: Rocket Draft FAQ: is it free, do you need an account, does it run on mobile, how RLCS ratings are calculated, special cards, regions and how the draft works.
faq.title: Rocket Draft FAQ
faq.intro: Quick answers to the questions players ask most about Rocket Draft — the free, fan-made RLCS draft game built on real Rocket League esports history.

sections.heading: Everything you need to get started
sections.body: Rocket Draft lets you draft a team from real historical RLCS lineups, build chemistry, collect special cards, and play an RLCS-style tournament — all in your browser, free, no account required. Below are the questions players ask most. If you want the full walkthrough, see How to Play; for the ratings system, see Ratings; for the legends showcase, see Special Cards.

faqs.q: Is Rocket Draft free?
faqs.a: Yes. Rocket Draft is completely free and non-commercial — a fan-made passion project celebrating RLCS history. There is no paywall, no ads required to play, and a "buy me a coffee" support link is entirely optional.

faqs.q: Do I need an account to play?
faqs.a: No account is needed. You can start a draft instantly and your progress is saved on your own device. Signing in is optional: an email code backs your progress up to the cloud and puts you on the global leaderboards.

faqs.q: Can I play on mobile?
faqs.a: Yes. Rocket Draft runs in any modern browser on both desktop and mobile — no app to download and no install.

faqs.q: Is Rocket Draft official or affiliated with an esports org?
faqs.a: No. Rocket Draft is an unofficial, fan-made project created by LiberatoRL. It is not affiliated with Psyonix, Epic Games, or any esports organization. Rocket League is a trademark of its owners. It was inspired by Rams' draftrlcs.app.

faqs.q: How are player ratings and overalls calculated?
faqs.a: Every overall is built in two layers: a calculated base plus a hand manual review. The calculation weighs team placement, tournament tier, season strength, win rate, titles, Major and Worlds appearances, Top 4 and Top 8 finishes, individual stats where available, region strength, and consistency across events. The manual review exists because esports data can mislead — some players overperform statistically due to context, others are historically elite despite worse team results (typical adjustment is small, around plus or minus 3, exceptional plus or minus 5). Six internal stats feed simulation and card depth: Offense, Defense, Mechanics, Consistency, Experience, and Clutch. See the Ratings page for the full methodology.

faqs.q: What are special cards?
faqs.a: Special cards are rare versions of players tied to iconic Rocket League esports moments — Worlds and Major MVP runs, legends, and signature plays. There are {specialCards} of them, and they can appear in any draft. Draft one and finish the run, win or lose, to unlock it in your collection forever. In-game, locked cards show as ??? until you unlock them. The Special Cards page is a curated showcase of legends and does not spoil your unlock progress.

faqs.q: How does the draft work?
faqs.a: Each round deals one real historical RLCS lineup. You take exactly one card from it — a player, the coach, the substitute, or the organization — until you have 3 players, 1 coach, 1 sub, and 1 org. The draft pool is fully random on every difficulty, so luck is the same for everyone; difficulty changes the tournament field, not your draw. If nothing in a lineup fits your open slots, the reroll is free.

faqs.q: What is SAM, the regional mode?
faqs.a: SAM is the South American region of Rocket League esports. In Rocket Draft it is also a Region-Locked Draft: the pool narrows to one scene's full depth — its World Championship teams plus the regional rosters that never reached Worlds, meaning deeper benches and local underdogs you won't see worldwide (for example, yanxnz). North America, Europe, MENA and Oceania have their own region-locked drafts too.

faqs.q: Are more players and teams being added?
faqs.a: Yes. The roster covers real RLCS lineups from 2016 to today, ratings are reviewed and updated over time, and APAC and Sub-Saharan Africa follow as region-locked drafts once their databases are deep enough. The community can also push back on ratings.

faqs.q: How is my progress saved?
faqs.a: Progress is saved locally on the device you play on — your collection, profile, and settings live in your browser, with no sign-in required. If you do sign in with your email, the same progress is backed up to the cloud and merged in, never lost.

faqs.q: Is Rocket Draft an RLCS draft game?
faqs.a: Yes. Rocket Draft is a free RLCS draft game and tournament simulator. You draft a roster from real RLCS lineups across every season since 2016, build team chemistry, and play an RLCS-style Swiss-into-double-elimination bracket — an RLCS draft you can run in the browser with no install.

faqs.q: What makes this RLCS draft different from a simple team picker?
faqs.a: Most RLCS draft tools just let you pick a lineup. Rocket Draft turns the RLCS draft into a full game: a chemistry system that rewards same-country, same-org and shared-history rosters, dozens of collectible special cards from famous Rocket League esports moments, four difficulties up to the all-time Legacy gauntlet, and a tournament that actually simulates to a champion. It is inspired by Rams' draftrlcs.app and expands the idea.

faqs.q: Can I do a region-locked RLCS draft (like a SAM / South America draft)?
faqs.a: Yes. Region-Locked Draft narrows the pool to one scene's full depth — its World Championship teams plus the regional rosters that never got there. North America, Europe, South America (SAM), MENA and Oceania are live, each a dedicated RLCS draft of that region's teams.

faqs.q: Is Rocket Draft a Rocket League simulator?
faqs.a: It simulates the esports side of Rocket League, not the car physics. You draft a roster from real RLCS lineups and the game simulates a 16-team tournament around it: a Swiss stage in best-of-5, then a double-elimination best-of-7 bracket, series by series, until one team wins the title.

faqs.q: Is Rocket Draft a fantasy RLCS league?
faqs.a: It is a fantasy-style draft, not a season-long fantasy league. There is no live scoring from real matches and no prizes: you draft from the whole history of the RLCS, and the tournament is simulated on the spot. The Daily Challenge gives everyone the same seeded draft to compare.

faqs.q: Is there a career or manager mode?
faqs.a: Yes. Road to Worlds is the career mode: you found a club, sign and develop real RLCS players, handle sponsors, wages and transfers, and play season after season of the RLCS calendar until you win the World Championship. It is free and runs in the browser like the draft.

ratings.metaTitle: RLCS Player Ratings — How Overalls Are Built
ratings.metaDescription: How Rocket Draft calculates RLCS player ratings: a calculated base plus a hand manual review, six internal stats, and why team overall stays the main factor.
ratings.title: How Rocket Draft Rates RLCS Players
ratings.intro: This is the transparent breakdown of how every player overall is built — the two layers behind the number, what the calculation weighs, and why some special cards rate above their base versions. If you have ever asked why a player carries the overall they do, this is the answer.

sections.heading: How overalls are built: base plus manual review
sections.body: Every player overall is built in two layers. First, a calculated base derived from results and context. Then a hand manual review — led by GWR, who balances the player ratings — because esports data misleads on its own. Some players overperform statistically due to context; others are historically elite despite worse team results. The manual adjustment is typically small — around ±3, with exceptional cases reaching ±5. The goal is a number that respects both the spreadsheet and the history.

sections.heading: What the calculation considers
sections.body: The calculated base weighs a wide spread of historical signal: team placement, tournament tier, season strength, win rate, titles, Major and Worlds appearances, Top 4 and Top 8 finishes, individual stats where available, region strength and context, and consistency across events. No single stat line decides an overall — the base reads the whole career arc across RLCS history from 2016 to today.

sections.heading: The six stats behind every card
sections.body: Six internal stats feed the match simulation and give cards their depth. Offense covers scoring and pressure. Defense is stability and avoiding bad losses. Mechanics is ceiling — the explosive, high-roll games. Consistency reduces collapse and variance. Experience rewards longer series and playoff runs. Clutch shows up in Game 5 and Game 7, overtime, and close series. Together they shape how a roster actually plays out.

sections.heading: Why special cards can beat base cards
sections.body: Special cards are rare versions tied to iconic Rocket League esports moments — Worlds and Major MVP runs, legends, signature plays. Because they capture a peak, a special card can rate above its base version. "Pinch God" (kuxir97, Season 2 World Champion and Worlds MVP) or "Four Times World Champion" (Turbopolsa) are not just reskins — the effect ramps with the moment. There are {specialCards} special cards to unlock by finishing a run with one drafted.

sections.heading: How team rating works: overall stays dominant
sections.body: A team rating is driven mostly by player overalls. Chemistry, org buffs, coach effects and special-card boosts add the edge — they never replace overall as the main factor. That said, a coherent, high-chemistry roster can beat a higher-rated all-star mix, so the top overall is not always the smart pick. On Hard and Legacy, chemistry is asymmetric: it helps your team while AI opponents bank no bonus.

sections.heading: How SAM and region players are rated
sections.body: Region-Locked Draft narrows the pool to one scene's full depth. South America (SAM) is live now, hand-researched from Liquipedia, covering Brazilian and South American teams — its World Championship rosters plus the regional Top 8 that never reached Worlds. Those players carry the same two-layer treatment, with region strength and context already folded into the base. A confirmed SAM name in the pool: yanxnz.

sections.heading: How often ratings are reviewed
sections.body: Ratings are not frozen. They are reviewed and updated over time as the methodology is refined and as history is re-read with fresh eyes. The community can push back on any overall — this page exists so those conversations start from a shared, honest baseline rather than a black box.

ratings.ctaLabel: Draft a team and see the overalls in action

strategy.metaTitle: Rocket Draft Strategy Guide — Best Picks & How to Win
strategy.metaDescription: A practical Rocket Draft strategy guide: best picks, how to build chemistry, when to value coach, sub and org, smart reroll use, and how to win on Hard and Legacy.
strategy.title: Rocket Draft Strategy Guide
strategy.intro: How to actually win in Rocket Draft: stars versus depth, building real chemistry, when to spend a slot on a coach, sub or org, smart reroll use, and the picks that carry you through Hard and Legacy.

sections.heading: Stars vs. depth: don't always take the top overall
sections.body: Team rating is driven mostly by your three players' overalls, but the highest-rated card is not always the right pick. Chemistry, org buffs, coach and special-card effects add the edge that decides close series. A coherent, high-chemistry roster can beat a higher-rated all-star mix. Before you grab the biggest number on the board, ask whether it fits your open slots and whether it links to the players you already hold.

sections.heading: How to build chemistry (the real edge)
sections.body: Chemistry is your main lever to out-punch a higher-rated field. The strongest link is three players from the same historical lineup; same country is strong; same organization counts. A coach or sub connected to your players, team or org adds a little more. Tiers run Poor, Okay, Good, Great, Perfect. Commit early to a country stack or a real lineup and the bonus compounds fast, so trade a sliver of raw overall for a roster that holds together.

sections.heading: When to value coach, sub and org
sections.body: Each lineup lets you take one card: a player, the coach, the substitute, or the organization. Players carry the rating, so they come first, but the support slots win tight matches. Take a coach or sub who shares a lineup or org with players you already drafted to bank extra chemistry. Pick an org that matches your players' historical org so the org-link bonus stacks. A connected support card is worth more than a slightly stronger but isolated one.

sections.heading: Using rerolls (and the free reroll)
sections.body: Rerolls differ by difficulty: Easy gives three, Normal gives one, Hard and Legacy give none. Spend them when a lineup offers nothing for your open slots, not to chase a marginally better card. One rule applies on every difficulty: if a dealt lineup has no card that fits your remaining slots, the reroll is free, so you never get stuck. On zero-reroll runs, plan your slots so you're rarely forced to take a dead card.

sections.heading: Difficulty-specific tips: Easy to Hard to Legacy
sections.body: Easy and Normal show overalls and forgive mistakes, so use them to learn the loop. Hard hides overalls, gives zero rerolls and fields a stronger bracket, rewarding historical knowledge: you draft on what you know about real RLCS rosters, not on numbers. Crucially, on Hard and Legacy chemistry is asymmetric, helping your team while AI opponents bank no chemistry bonus, so a tightly linked stack is your equalizer. Legacy unlocks by winning on Hard and is an all-time gauntlet of championship rosters.

sections.heading: Reading special cards
sections.body: Special cards are rare versions tied to iconic Rocket League esports moments, like "Pinch God" (kuxir97) or "Four Times World Champion" (Turbopolsa). They can appear in any draft on any difficulty, can rate above their base versions, and ramp in effect from legends to MVP cards to moments. Draft one and finish the run, win or lose, to unlock it in your collection forever. When a special fits your roster and chemistry plan, it is usually worth the slot for both the edge and the unlock.

strategy.ctaLabel: Start a draft and put the strategy to work

special-cards.metaTitle: RLCS Special Cards — Rocket League Card Collection
special-cards.metaDescription: A showcase of {specialCards} RLCS special cards in Rocket Draft — rare versions tied to iconic Rocket League esports moments. Draft one, finish the run, unlock it forever.
special-cards.title: RLCS Special Cards
special-cards.intro: Special cards are the rare, collectible side of Rocket Draft — versions of real players tied to the biggest moments in RLCS history. There are {specialCards} to chase, and every one is earned the same way: draft it, finish the run, keep it forever.

sections.heading: What special cards are
sections.body: Special cards are rare versions of real players tied to iconic Rocket League esports moments — Worlds and Major MVP runs, era-defining legends, signature plays. They can appear in ANY draft, on any difficulty, because the pool is always fully random. A special often rates above the player's base card and carries a stronger effect, so pulling one mid-run can reshape the whole roster you were building.

sections.heading: How you unlock them
sections.body: The rule is simple: draft the special card into your lineup, then FINISH the run — win or lose, it doesn't matter. Complete the tournament with that card on your team and it unlocks in your Collection permanently. There's no grind and no account required; you just have to see the run through. Until you unlock one, it shows in-game as ??? — discovering them is part of the play.

sections.heading: Rarities and effects
sections.body: Special cards ramp in effect by tier — legends, MVP cards, and standout moments scale up as you climb the rarity ladder. Effects are direct attribute boosts that feed the same six internal stats every card uses: Offense, Defense, Mechanics, Consistency, Experience, and Clutch. The higher the tier, the bigger the edge it brings to your team rating, which is why a well-placed special can lift a roster above a stronger-looking field.

sections.heading: A few legendary examples
sections.body: The names on this showcase are the ones the community remembers. "The Mountain" is Kronovi, the Season 1 champion and one of the first defining superstars of the scene. "Pinch God" is kuxir97, Season 2 World Champion and Worlds MVP. "Four Times World Champion" is Turbopolsa, owner of four RLCS World Championships. These are the kind of legends a special card exists to celebrate.

sections.heading: How they fit the draft
sections.body: A special card is never a free win — your team rating is driven mostly by player overalls, with chemistry, org buffs, coaches, and special effects adding the edge on top. The smart play is fitting a special into a lineup that already has overall and chemistry, not chasing a shiny card into a roster that doesn't hold together. Use one to sharpen a build, and let the run decide whether it joins your Collection.

sections.heading: {specialCards} to collect — with the mystery intact
sections.body: There are {specialCards} special cards in all, and the in-game Collection keeps its mystery: locked cards stay as ??? until you earn them, so your unlock progress is yours alone. This page is a public, curated showcase of the legends — a celebration of RLCS history, not a spoiler dump. Head to Play, draft a real historical lineup, and start hunting your first one.

special-cards.ctaLabel: Start a draft and hunt special cards

sam.metaTitle: SAM Rocket League — South America's RLCS Region
sam.metaDescription: What SAM means in Rocket League esports: the South American RLCS region, its Brazilian-led teams, and a free draft locked to 100+ hand-researched SAM lineups.
sam.title: SAM Rocket League — South America's Region
sam.intro: SAM is the South American region of Rocket League esports. Rocket Draft covers it in depth: a hand-researched database of Brazilian and South American RLCS lineups, and a Region-Locked Draft that deals from nothing else — free in your browser.

sections.heading: What SAM means in Rocket League
sections.body: SAM stands for South America. It is one of the regions of the Rocket League Championship Series, next to North America (NA), Europe (EU), Oceania (OCE), the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), Asia-Pacific (APAC) and Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Each region runs its own qualifiers and regional events, and its best teams earn the region's places at the international Majors and the World Championship. The SAM scene is led by Brazil, with players and teams from Argentina, Chile and the rest of the continent alongside. Organizations such as FURIA, Team Secret, KRÜ Esports, MIBR, w7m esports, INTZ and Ninjas in Pyjamas have all fielded SAM rosters, and every one of them is in the game.

sections.heading: SAM in the Rocket Draft database
sections.body: The SAM database holds {SAM.lineups} lineups from {SAM.orgs} organizations and {SAM.players} players, across {SAM.seasons} seasons from {SAM.firstSeason} to {SAM.lastSeason}. The team and player pages list each of them season by season.

sections.heading: What the SAM region-locked draft is
sections.body: SAM is a Region-Locked Draft: instead of pulling from the global pool, every round deals from South America's full depth. You still draft the same way — take one card per lineup until you have 3 players, 1 coach, 1 sub and 1 org — but every card comes from the SAM scene. South America was the first region live, hand-researched from Liquipedia, covering Brazilian and South American teams from RLCS history.

sections.heading: What's in the SAM pool
sections.body: The pool combines two layers of the region: its World Championship teams, and the regional Top 8 that never reached Worlds. That second layer is the difference — deeper benches, local heroes and cult underdogs you won't see in the worldwide draft. Confirmed Brazilian names like yanxnz live in here. It's the region's real depth, not just its Worlds highlight reel.

sections.heading: Why it's a differentiator
sections.body: Most RLCS draft games stop at the World Championship lineups. SAM goes deeper, surfacing the regional Top 8 that never made it to a Worlds stage — the qualifier teams, the near-misses, the scene's full bench. For Brazilian and South American fans that means drafting the players you actually watched, not only the handful who reached the global stage. That regional depth is what sets Rocket Draft apart.

sections.heading: How region-lock changes a run
sections.body: Region-lock changes only the pool — nothing else. Your difficulty, chemistry rules and the full RLCS-style tournament all play exactly as normal: 16 teams, a Swiss stage into double-elimination playoffs. Same-country chemistry naturally lands more often inside one scene, so a coherent SAM roster can punch above a scattered all-star mix. The draft luck stays random; only the names on the cards are SAM.

sections.heading: Every region, one scene at a time
sections.body: South America went live first because it was hand-researched and ready. Since Season 1, North America, Europe, MENA and Oceania are live too, each built the same way — a scene's international teams plus the regional rosters that never reached a World Championship. APAC and Sub-Saharan Africa follow as their databases grow. The goal stays the same: let every fan lock the draft to the scene they grew up watching.

sam.ctaLabel: Play the SAM Rocket League draft

simulator.metaTitle: Rocket League Simulator — Free RLCS Tournament Sim
simulator.metaDescription: A free Rocket League esports simulator in your browser: draft a roster from RLCS history and simulate a 16-team RLCS tournament, Swiss stage to grand final.
simulator.title: Rocket League Esports Simulator
simulator.intro: Rocket Draft is a free Rocket League simulator for the esports side of the game. You build a roster from real RLCS lineups, and the game simulates a full RLCS-style tournament around it, series by series, until one team lifts the trophy.

sections.heading: What this Rocket League simulator simulates
sections.body: It does not simulate car physics or a match on the pitch. It simulates the competition: rosters, ratings, series and brackets. Every card is a real player, coach, substitute or organization from RLCS history, 2016 to today. Each player carries an overall and six internal stats — Offense, Defense, Mechanics, Consistency, Experience and Clutch — reviewed by hand, and those numbers decide how a series plays out.

sections.heading: How the RLCS tournament simulation works
sections.body: Sixteen teams enter. The Swiss stage is played in best-of-5: three wins advance, three losses and you are out. The top eight seed into a double-elimination bracket in best-of-7, where an upper-bracket loss drops you to the lower bracket, not out of the event. Your team rating comes mostly from player overalls; chemistry, the organization's buff, the coach and special-card effects add the edge. Upsets are part of the model: a lower-rated team can still take a series.

sections.heading: Simulate at your own pace
sections.body: Play the tournament one series at a time and read how each one went, or skip to the end and go straight to the final standings. Either way the results screen breaks down the run: where you finished, who knocked you out, and how your roster rated.

sections.heading: Four difficulties, one fair draft
sections.body: Easy, Normal and Hard scale the strength of the field you simulate against. The draft itself is fully random on every difficulty, so luck is the same for everyone. Clearing Hard unlocks Legacy: an all-time gauntlet of championship rosters, with overalls hidden so that knowledge of the scene does the work.

sections.heading: Simulate one region or the whole world
sections.body: The worldwide draft mixes every region and era. Region-Locked Draft narrows both the cards you are dealt and the teams in the bracket to a single scene: North America, Europe, South America (SAM), MENA or Oceania, each with the regional rosters that never reached a World Championship.

sections.heading: From one tournament to a whole career
sections.body: Road to Worlds stretches the simulation across seasons. You found a club, sign real RLCS players, train them, balance wages and sponsors, and play the calendar of regional events, Majors and the World Championship while the rest of the world is simulated around you.

sections.heading: Free, in the browser
sections.body: There is nothing to download and no account to create. Rocket Draft runs in any modern browser on desktop and mobile, and your progress is saved on your device. It is a fan-made project, not affiliated with Psyonix or Epic Games.

faqs.q: Is there a free Rocket League simulator?
faqs.a: Yes. Rocket Draft is free and runs in the browser. It simulates Rocket League esports tournaments — you draft a roster from RLCS history and the bracket is simulated series by series.

faqs.q: Can I simulate an RLCS tournament?
faqs.a: Yes. Every run ends in a simulated RLCS-style event: 16 teams, a Swiss stage in best-of-5 and a double-elimination playoff bracket in best-of-7, against real historical lineups.

faqs.q: Does it simulate real Rocket League gameplay?
faqs.a: No. There are no cars or physics here. The simulation works on team and player ratings, chemistry and series formats, the way a sports management game does.

manager.metaTitle: Rocket League Manager Game & Career Simulator
manager.metaDescription: Road to Worlds is a free Rocket League manager game: found a club, sign real RLCS players, train them, run sponsors and finances, and win the World Championship.
manager.title: Road to Worlds — Rocket League Manager Game
manager.intro: Road to Worlds is Rocket Draft's career mode: a free Rocket League esports manager game that runs in your browser. Found a club, build a squad from real RLCS players, and take it from regional qualifiers to the World Championship, one season at a time.

sections.heading: Found your club
sections.body: A career starts with an empty club. Pick the region you want to compete in, name the organization, design its crest and colours, and choose a difficulty. The difficulty sets your starting budget and how forgiving the finances are. Then you sign your first roster and the season begins.

sections.heading: A full RLCS calendar
sections.body: The career opens in RLCS Season X and runs through every season to 2026. Each season is split into regional events with open qualifiers; regional points send the best teams to the Majors, and season points decide who reaches the World Championship. Open weeks offer community cups and invitationals. If the title has not come by the end of 2026, the career can continue into an endless mode with new seasons.

sections.heading: Sign, train and develop players
sections.body: The transfer market works in windows, with fees, wages, contracts and rival bids. Your squad holds four players — three starters and a substitute. Training targets individual attributes, coaches shape how fast players grow, and real RLCS coaches appear on the coach market. Players improve with matches and training, and decline as the years pass, so a roster has to be renewed.

sections.heading: Run the business
sections.body: Prize money, sponsors and reputation pay for the squad. Wages, staff and transfer fees take it away. The Finances screen shows the weekly statement and the projection for the season, and loans are there when the balance turns red. Support staff — an assistant coach, an opponent analyst, a physical trainer and a brand manager — each help in one area.

sections.heading: A simulated world that keeps moving
sections.body: Every other club plays its own season. Results in all regions are simulated week by week, rivals sign and sell players, and the standings and the title history record every Major and World Championship winner, starting from the real champions of the early RLCS seasons.

sections.heading: Same data as the draft
sections.body: Road to Worlds uses the same hand-reviewed database as the draft game: real players, coaches and organizations from RLCS history, with the same overalls and stats. It is free, needs no download, and saves on your device.

faqs.q: Is there a Rocket League manager game?
faqs.a: Road to Worlds, the career mode of Rocket Draft, is a free fan-made Rocket League esports manager game. You run a club: signings, training, finances and the RLCS calendar.

faqs.q: Is the Rocket League career simulator free?
faqs.a: Yes. It is free, runs in the browser on desktop and mobile, and needs no download or account.

faqs.q: Does it use real RLCS players and teams?
faqs.a: Yes. The player and coach market is built from the same database of real RLCS lineups, from 2016 to today, that the draft game uses.

sections.heading: Fantasy Rocket League without waiting for match day
sections.body: A classic fantasy league needs a live season, a group of friends and weeks of patience. Rocket Draft is a single-player fantasy draft you can finish in a few minutes: draft a roster, watch it play a full RLCS-style bracket, and start again with different picks.

sections.heading: How the fantasy draft works
sections.body: Each round deals one real historical RLCS lineup and you take exactly one card from it — a player, the coach, the substitute or the organization — until you hold three players, a coach, a sub and an org. Nobody picks the same pool twice: the lineups are random on every run, so the skill is reading what each one offers.

sections.heading: All-time rosters, not only this season's
sections.body: The database covers RLCS lineups from 2016 to today. You can put a Season 1 champion next to a current star, and chemistry decides whether it works: players from the same lineup, the same country or the same organization lift each other, so a coherent team can beat a pile of big names.

sections.heading: What it is not
sections.body: Rocket Draft is not a season-long fantasy league. There is no live scoring from real matches, no private leagues and no prizes or money of any kind. It is a free, fan-made game about the history of the scene.

sections.heading: The same draft for everyone, once a day
sections.body: The Daily Challenge is the closest thing to a league: one seeded draft per day, the same lineups for every player, with a streak to defend. Signing in is optional and puts your best rosters on the global leaderboards.

sections.heading: Free, in the browser
sections.body: No download and no account are needed. Rocket Draft runs in any modern browser on desktop and mobile, and your collection and progress are saved on your device.

faqs.q: Is there a fantasy game for Rocket League esports?
faqs.a: Rocket Draft is a free fantasy-style draft for Rocket League esports: you pick players from real RLCS lineups and the game simulates a tournament with your roster.

faqs.q: Does RLCS fantasy here use live match results?
faqs.a: No. Nothing depends on real upcoming matches. The draft uses historical lineups and the bracket is simulated immediately.
